name: How do I make a tiny pantry hold more without turning into a mess?

mainEntity.name: How do I make a tiny pantry hold more without turning into a mess?

acceptedAnswer.text: A small pantry can work well when storage is shallow, adjustable, and divided by use. Elite Remodeling & Design may consider pull-out shelves, deep lower drawers, door storage, and floor-to-ceiling cabinetry so items are visible instead of buried behind one another. Typical pantry shelves are often around 14–16 inches deep, while high shelves may be shallower for easier reach; the final dimensions should follow your containers and available space. Reserve lower storage for heavier appliances or bulk goods, and place everyday items between waist and eye level. Measure cereal boxes, small appliances, paper goods, and the largest containers before selecting shelf spacing. Avoid making every shelf the same depth if that creates wasted space or difficult access.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use adjustable shelves, pull-outs, door storage, and deep lower drawers instead of relying on one uniform shelf depth.
